newsitem.title: UK: Gehe tells Lloyds' investors to go for cash.
newsitem.headline: Gehe tells Lloyds' investors to go for cash.

text.p: Germany's Gehe AG, battling with rival UniChem Plc for control of British pharmacy group Lloyds Chemists Plc, urged Lloyds' shareholders to avoid risk by accepting its cash offer.
Gehe's comments followed a letter to shareholders from Lloyds telling them to take no action as the two bidders might still increase their offers.
Gehe's latest cash bid values Lloyds at 650.6 million stg, while UniChem has made a cash and share bid valuing Lloyds at 657.6 million.

Gehe said its all-cash offer gave shareholders a risk-free option, whereas UniChem's predominantly share offer "exposed shareholders to the risks of adverse developments in the UK pharmacy market, an unstable stock market and interest rate developments".
Gehe said the value of UniChem's offer had fallen and "at 484 pence per Lloyds Chemists share, is currently worth 16 pence less than Gehe's cash offer of 500 pence".
Gehe management board chairman Dieter Kammerer said: "I believe our cash offer has become increasingly attractive."
Both UniChem and Gehe, who have been fighting for control of Lloyds since February this year, have until January 17 to increase their offers. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
